themes.name: other: unexpected_charge
themes.problem_statement: Statements about unexpected charge that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Auto loan payoff higher than quoted
themes.problem_statement: The final payoff amount for an auto loan or lease buyout is hundreds of dollars higher than previously specified or expected, with no explanation provided.
themes.root_cause: Errors in the calculation logic or communication of the final auto loan/lease payoff amount cause discrepancies between the quoted amount and actual amount due.
examples: The payoff calculation for buying out a leased vehicle was $480.00 more than what the lease specified, and Chase has not returned calls, messages or letters about the discrepancy.

themes.name: Unwanted products or fees added to auto loan
themes.problem_statement: Thousands of dollars in unwanted insurance, tire/wheel coverage, or service fees are added to an auto loan without clear disclosure or customer consent.
themes.root_cause: The sales or loan origination process allows optional products and fees to be bundled into the loan without requiring explicit customer agreement or disclosure.
examples: XXXX insurance, tire/wheel coverage, and thousands of dollars in service fees were added to the loan without clear disclosure or the option to decline.
$5000.00 in products the customer told the salesman they did not want was added to the loan, and it took getting the run-around between departments to have it removed.

themes.name: Auto loan autopay withdrew incorrect amount
themes.problem_statement: An automatic payment for an auto loan withdraws a significantly higher amount than what is actually owed, especially for the final payoff payment.
themes.root_cause: The automatic payment system fails to adjust for the actual remaining balance on final loan payments, pulling a default or incorrect amount.
examples: The final auto-pay loan payment withdrew $450.00 instead of the $120.00 actually owed, with no notice that the higher amount would be taken.

themes.name: Unexpected overdraft or NSF fees
themes.problem_statement: Customers are charged high overdraft, insufficient funds (NSF), or low balance fees, even when they haven't used their cards or only overdrew accidentally.
themes.root_cause: The transaction posting order or fee assessment logic unfairly penalizes customers, or processes fees on inactive accounts or without opt-in consent.
examples: The customer was charged high overdraft and NSF fees after accidentally overdrawing their account a couple of times.
The customer's checking account is incurring multiple fees, such as overdrafts, out-of-network ATM fees, and low balance fees, causing frustration.

themes.name: Incorrect monthly maintenance fees
themes.problem_statement: Customers are double-charged monthly maintenance fees or charged fees for not meeting minimum balances, feeling penalized for holding money in the account.
themes.root_cause: A system error processes monthly service charges twice, or fails to correctly apply fee waivers based on the customer's account balance and activity.
examples: The customer was overcharged for their monthly maintenance fee on their statement.
A $20 monthly maintenance fee was incorrectly charged as $40 due to a system error that charged the fee twice.

themes.name: Unjustified interest and late fees
themes.problem_statement: Customers are charged interest or late fees despite paying before the statement closes, or because login issues prevented them from making a payment.
themes.root_cause: Interest calculation and fee assessment logic fails to account for processing delays, login outages, or the precise timing of statement closing dates.
examples: A $34.00 interest charge was applied because $530.00 of the statement balance was paid one day after the minimum due date, even though it was paid two days before the statement cycle closed.
Being unable to log in has already caused one late fee and risks another, along with a possible negative credit report mark.

themes.name: Unexpected foreign transaction fees
themes.problem_statement: Customers are charged 3% foreign transaction fees on purchases they believed were domestic, or face large fees abroad after changing account types.
themes.root_cause: Merchant category coding or payment network routing misclassifies domestic transactions as foreign, or fee structures are not properly disclosed upon product changes.
examples: A 3% fee was charged for using a debit card at a merchant, though debit card purchases should not carry that fee.
A $39.00 foreign transaction fee was charged on a purchase believed to be domestic, with no notice from the merchant or Chase beforehand.

themes.name: Purchases incorrectly coded as cash advances
themes.problem_statement: Normal purchases, like charity donations, are processed as cash advances, triggering immediate $10 fees and high daily interest without warning.
themes.root_cause: Transaction mapping rules incorrectly categorize specific merchants or payment platforms as cash advances, applying immediate fees and interest.
examples: A $92.00 charity purchase was charged a $10.00 cash-like transaction fee and coded as a cash advance subject to nearly 30% daily interest, with no way to pay off just that portion.
After forgetting to toggle the purchases tab on two payments, cash advance fees and interest were applied; the fees were refunded but the $18.00 interest was not.

themes.name: Un-refunded or unexpected annual fees
themes.problem_statement: Customers are billed $95 to $550 annual fees without prior notice on previously free cards, or the bank refuses to refund fees after accounts are closed.
themes.root_cause: Fee billing processes fail to notify customers of new fees, and system rules do not automatically prorate or refund annual fees when accounts are closed.
examples: Chase kept the full $550.00 annual fee even though the account was closed by the bank only months later.
A card that had never carried an annual fee began being billed $95.00 with no prior notification, and Chase refused to refund the fees already charged with no explanation.

themes.name: Overcharges and hidden fees on travel bookings
themes.problem_statement: Customers using the bank's travel portal are double-charged for car rentals, face excessive $370 cancellation fees, or airlines show no payment at the gate.
themes.root_cause: The travel portal's integration with third-party vendors miscalculates fees, fails to sync payments to merchants, or applies incorrect markup/cancellation rules.
examples: A one-day rental booked through Chase's own travel portal for $310.00 already included the different-location return fee, but the rental company charged $170.00 for it again.
Chase Travel charged a $370.00 cancellation fee, more than ten times the airline's advertised $30.00 fee for flights originating in the US, and this discrepancy was not disclosed at booking.

themes.name: Fees on closed or paid credit accounts
themes.problem_statement: Interest, late fees, and annual fees of $75 to $550 continue to accrue or are billed on credit accounts that have been fully paid off or closed.
themes.root_cause: The system fails to halt fee generation and interest accrual after an account status is updated to closed or fully paid off.
examples: After paying off and closing a credit card, Chase continued adding interest and late fees for over eight months with no online access or adequate notice, only discovered through a mortgage credit check.
Chase refused to refund the $550.00 Sapphire Reserve annual fee even though the card was closed with 5 months of paid benefits remaining.

themes.name: Merchant billing error
themes.problem_statement: Merchants charge more than authorized, apply unauthorized recurring charges, or rebill for items that were already returned and refunded.
themes.root_cause: Merchant processing systems or apps have bugs that alter authorization amounts or fail to correctly process cancellations and returns.
examples: The customer discovered a rebill for two items that were returned unopened using the store's own return label and already refunded, with no notification of the new charge.
A merchant app has a bug that charges more than authorized, for example $63.00 charged when only $56.00 was authorized, and this has happened on every order.

themes.name: Unexpected interest despite timely payment
themes.problem_statement: Customers are charged interest despite paying the full balance before the due date, due to undisclosed daily accrual or promotional period rules.
themes.root_cause: Interest calculation rules, such as daily accrual or promotional balance allocations, are applied in a way that is hidden from the payment dashboard.
examples: After paying the full balance before the due date, an $85.00 interest charge appeared, and nowhere on the account dashboard or payment page was it disclosed that interest accrues daily even with early full payment.
During the advertised 0% APR year, payments of $ XXXX to $500.00 did not reduce the balance transfer amount, suggesting hidden fees were being charged that were never disclosed.

themes.name: Late fee due to payment processing issue
themes.problem_statement: Customers are charged late fees or returned payment fees because scheduled payments or point redemptions fail to process correctly on the bank's end.
themes.root_cause: Bank system errors in processing scheduled automatic payments, point redemptions, or electronic fund transfers lead to missed payments and late fees.
examples: Redeeming points plus a payment from checking was used to cover the amount due, but a late fee was charged the very next day.
While locked out of the account, three late credit card payment fees were charged, lowering the customer's credit score.

themes.name: Fees/interest on disputed or fraudulent charges
themes.problem_statement: Late fees and interest continue to accrue on charges that customers have already reported as fraudulent, identity theft, or are actively disputing.
themes.root_cause: The dispute resolution process fails to freeze associated charges, allowing the billing system to continue generating interest and late fees on disputed amounts.
examples: Late fees and interest keep adding up on what is likely a fraudulent initial charge on the account, which the family cannot verify or dispute.
Despite filing disputes over identity-theft-related credit card charges, the bank continues calling for payment and adding late fees and interest.

themes.name: other: money_held_or_not_returned
themes.problem_statement: Statements about money held or not returned that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Account frozen due to bank setup error
themes.problem_statement: Accounts holding over $14,000 are frozen and placed under OFAC control because a banker mistakenly checked a nationality-related box during setup.
themes.root_cause: Employee input errors during account setup trigger automated compliance and fraud flags, leading to system-enforced account freezes.
examples: A banker who admitted responsibility mistakenly checked a nationality-related box when opening three accounts totaling over $14000.00, leading to escalating restrictions and an eventual freeze under OFAC control.

themes.name: Missing check cashed due to failure to freeze
themes.problem_statement: A $6,900 missing cashier's check is cashed by an unauthorized person because the bank failed to cancel or freeze it after multiple reports.
themes.root_cause: Process failures or delays in the stop-payment system prevent agents from successfully freezing a cashier's check when reported missing.
examples: A $6,900.00 cashier's check marked as delivered was never received, and despite reporting this multiple times, the bank did not cancel or freeze it before it was cashed by someone else.

themes.name: Funds not returned after account closure
themes.problem_statement: Funds from a closed account are not returned to the customer as promised or expected.
themes.root_cause: Bank process failure to properly disburse remaining funds after account closure, or internal delays/errors.
examples: After Chase confirmed by phone that the check endorser was verified, the back office still denied releasing the funds from the closed account.
Checking and savings accounts were closed without notice, and a promised $630.00 balance was not mailed within the stated 10 business days.

themes.name: Funds held indefinitely due to verification issues
themes.problem_statement: Social Security or $170k IRS deposits are held and accounts frozen pending third-party verifications that fail due to old phone numbers or unsupported methods.
themes.root_cause: Rigid fraud verification processes rely on third-party systems or outdated data, preventing agents from manually releasing valid government deposits.
examples: After the bank closed the account for suspected identity theft and confirmed the customer's identity, it continued withholding a legitimate Social Security deposit pending verification from the Treasury Department, despi

A $170,000.00 IRS employee retention credit check deposited into a new business account led Chase's fraud team to close the account, and even after paying $300.00 for a required address change, the promised release never

themes.name: ATM cash/check deposit malfunction
themes.problem_statement: Funds deposited via ATM are not credited to the account due to ATM malfunction, and resolution is delayed or denied.
themes.root_cause: ATM hardware or software malfunction leading to uncredited deposits, compounded by difficult or unresolved investigation processes.
examples: A $2,900.00 cash deposit made at a Chase ATM never appeared in the account, and a temporary credit issued during the investigation was later reversed after an audit found no discrepancy.

A $300.00 cash deposit that an ATM froze on and failed to post, confirmed by the bank as a machine error at the time, was later reversed after an investigation concluded it was processed as authorized.

themes.name: ATM deposit malfunction with funds reversed or held
themes.problem_statement: Cash deposits of $1,400 to $7,000 get stuck in malfunctioning ATMs, and temporary credits are reversed without adequate review of surveillance footage.
themes.root_cause: ATM hardware fails mid-transaction, and the back-office reconciliation process fails to verify the cash overage or review security footage.
examples: A $7000.00 cash deposit at a Chase ATM got stuck in the machine and has not been returned.
A $1400.00 temporary credit for an ATM deposit that errored mid-transaction was reversed after Chase claimed its investigation found no ATM error or extra funds.

themes.name: Account closed and remaining balance not returned
themes.problem_statement: Customer's account was closed, but the bank has not returned the remaining balance or a promised refund check for up to a month.
themes.root_cause: Delays, errors, or failures in the back-office process for issuing and mailing balance refund checks following account closure.
examples: Deposited checks were flagged as fraud and the account was frozen then closed, but no balance check has been issued nearly a month later, and the freeze also blocked an automatic credit card payment causing new interest.
Chase closed the account, leaving the customer with no access to funds while the check remains unverified.

themes.name: Check deposit held due to verification failure
themes.problem_statement: A deposited check of up to $25,000 is held or the account frozen because the bank claims it cannot verify the check or the issuer's identity via phone.
themes.root_cause: Risk policies require phone verification of checks or issuers, failing when the issuer is unreachable, lacks a matching number, or uses a third-party service.
examples: Chase will only verify a cleared and available employer check by calling a number that reaches a building security guard who cannot confirm anything, and refuses any alternate way to verify it.
Chase has withheld $25,000.00 for over a month citing the need to verify a deposited check, but has taken no action to verify it.

themes.name: Funds frozen indefinitely for suspicious activity
themes.problem_statement: Funds up to $3,900 are held or the account is frozen for an extended period for 'review' or 'suspicious activity' with no timeline provided.
themes.root_cause: Fraud algorithms or compliance reviews flag an account, and the internal investigation process is bottlenecked or lacks an efficient resolution mechanism.
examples: A tax refund check made out only to the customer was placed on a multi-day hold with none of the funds made available, longer than a two-day hold a different bank applied to a similar non-government check.
After verifying a cleared fraud flag, all business accounts were frozen and are being closed within 10 business days with no reason given.

themes.name: Check held due to failed phone verification
themes.problem_statement: A deposited check is held or the account frozen because the bank cannot verify the check via phone.
themes.root_cause: The bank's verification procedures require confirming the check via a specific phone number (often public records), which fails or is unavailable.
examples: A $1500.00 check, endorsed by both payees and checked by the teller at deposit, has been held for over a year because Chase could not complete phone verification of one payee.

A $50000.00 cashier's check deposited at the daughter's bank was flagged as invalid by phone, but despite the issuing bank confirming it is valid, it will not provide the written verification the receiving bank requires

themes.name: Extended freeze for fraud or suspicious activity review
themes.problem_statement: Customer's account and funds are frozen for weeks or months without explanation or resolution.
themes.root_cause: The bank's fraud or risk department placed a restriction or hold for investigation and is delaying the release of funds beyond standard timeframes.
examples: The entire account has been frozen for nearly a month during the fraud review, cutting off access to paychecks and deposits and causing financial hardship.

Chase withdrew the funds from an insurance check made out to the customer and mechanic but hasn't released them, citing an unexplained missing verification, while also refusing to return the funds to the insurer.

themes.name: Funds frozen due to legal order or levy
themes.problem_statement: Customer's funds were frozen or seized due to a claimed debt, levy, or court order.
themes.root_cause: The bank applied a legal hold or levy to the account without proper notice or release, sometimes affecting protected or exempt funds.
examples: Chase allowed a legal hold on the customer's custodial account to satisfy the parent's legal fees, even though the funds were the customer's own money from employment and they were never notified or a defendant.
Chase confirmed receiving the state levy release but is still holding all funds in the account and could not explain why it has not been processed.

themes.name: Account funds frozen or restricted without clear reason
themes.problem_statement: Funds in customer's account (new, existing, or closed) are frozen, restricted, or withheld without clear justification, explanation, or timeline for release.
themes.root_cause: Bank's internal risk/fraud policies or system incorrectly flagged the account, or bank failed to communicate the reason/resolution clearly.
examples: A hold was placed on two business checks totaling $56,000.00 until a set date, restricting the customer's ability to operate their business and meet a client deadline.
The customer's account was frozen while the fraud claims were being processed, adding stress on top of the scam loss.

themes.name: Check deposit hold extended without justification
themes.problem_statement: A hold on a check deposit (e.g., $30,000) is unilaterally extended past promised availability dates or federal guidelines without written notice or justification.
themes.root_cause: Deposit holds are extended without proper notice or justification due to internal verification delays or failure to adhere to promised availability dates.
examples: A check deposit hold was extended past its promised availability date without any new written notice, pushing the account over $5,000 negative.

A settlement check deposit stayed locked well past the 10-day federal hold guideline, with different representatives giving conflicting confirmations about whether the law firm verification was already completed.

themes.name: Funds incorrectly garnished or frozen by court order
themes.problem_statement: Up to $27,000 is garnished or frozen based on an incorrect legal order against a non-owner, or lacking proper notice, causing negative balances.
themes.root_cause: Incorrect application of a legal order (e.g., garnishment) due to identity mismatch, lack of proper jurisdiction, or failure to verify legal standing.
examples: A garnishment took funds and a legal fee for a debt cleared by the state, and the bank sent the payment anyway after receiving the release letter, refusing a stop-payment request.
A federal SSA check deposit was apparently garnished with no legal notice provided, causing automated transactions to be returned negatively for 7 days.

themes.name: Funds unrecovered in fraud or theft cases
themes.problem_statement: Up to $8,200 is lost due to stolen or unauthorized checks, and the bank fails to recover funds, denies provisional credit, or closes cases prematurely.
themes.root_cause: Fraud investigation or recovery processes are ineffective or incomplete, leading to unrecovered funds and denial of provisional credit.
examples: A mailed business check was stolen and deposited at another bank, and despite Chase's promise to recover the funds, the other bank hasn't responded and Chase plans to close the case.
Despite prompt reporting and a submitted affidavit, the funds from the first altered check remain debited with no provisional credit.

themes.name: Cleared check funds held indefinitely
themes.problem_statement: Funds from a check that has already cleared remain on an unexplained or extended hold, preventing customer access.
themes.root_cause: Bank's internal holding procedures, system errors, or lack of proper review keep legitimate and cleared funds inaccessible.
examples: A check from selling a car was suspended and remains suspended even though it has already cleared and the funds were received.
A nearly $230,000.00 check, confirmed valid by the issuing company, has been held for over 10 days with no clear or real explanation given by any representative.

themes.name: Account restriction blocks access to legitimate funds
themes.problem_statement: Customers cannot access funds (e.g., $5,200) due to unexpected account restrictions or closures, causing direct deposits to bounce or be returned.
themes.root_cause: Flaws in account restriction or closure processes, internal holds, or verification procedures incorrectly withhold legitimate customer funds.
examples: During the restriction, direct deposits bounced, an IRS refund was returned requiring a months-long wait for a paper check, and another payment bounced, causing fees.
A personal account was closed with no clear explanation, and about $5,200 in remaining funds has not been released despite requests for a timeline.

themes.name: Funds escheated to incorrect state or address
themes.problem_statement: Over $120,000 in cashier's checks is escheated to an incorrect state or address without prior legally required pre-escheatment notification.
themes.root_cause: The escheatment process relies on incorrect customer address data or fails to execute legally required pre-escheatment notice procedures.
examples: $120000.00 in cashier's checks were escheated to Ohio instead of the customer's Florida address on file, with no pre-escheatment notice ever sent, and misleading 'void after 7 years' language on the checks.

themes.name: Earned rewards forfeited upon account closure
themes.problem_statement: Up to $1,400 in earned rewards points or statement credits are confiscated immediately when an account is closed without notice or chance to redeem.
themes.root_cause: System automatically forfeits earned rewards or credits upon account closure without allowing a grace period for customer redemption.
examples: Chase closed the account without a clear reason and immediately forfeited $1,400.00 in rewards with no chance to redeem them.
Chase confiscated already-earned Ultimate Rewards points when it closed the account, even though the account was in good standing.

themes.name: Delayed or withheld credit balance refunds
themes.problem_statement: Overpayments or credit balances up to $13,000 are not refunded, significantly delayed for weeks, or partially withheld despite cleared funds.
themes.root_cause: Inefficient refund processing, unexplained internal holds on funds, or a lack of transparent communication regarding credit balance disposition.
examples: Part of a duplicate payment overpayment was withheld against a balance that wasn't due yet, taking two weeks to return with no interest paid on the held funds.
A duplicate $5,200 payment created a $4,400 credit balance that Chase has failed to refund across three calls, each with a different explanation.

themes.name: Promised statement credits or refunds not received
themes.problem_statement: Promised statement credits (e.g., $150 for benefits) or reimbursements up to $770 are not applied to the account even after 6 months of waiting.
themes.root_cause: System failure to apply promised credits or refunds, or miscommunication and failure in payment issuance or delivery for manual reimbursements.
examples: A $150.00 statement credit for an activated card benefit never posted despite a qualifying purchase made more than three weeks earlier.
A $320.00 charge for canceled services has not been refunded weeks after being promised, despite attempting to resolve it directly with the merchant.

themes.name: Misdirected or lost funds during wire transfers
themes.problem_statement: Wire transfers up to $33,000 are sent to the wrong account or held in an incompatible account, and the bank fails to automatically return or recall the funds.
themes.root_cause: Errors in routing or processing funds by the bank or network, or an inability to recover funds sent to an incorrect recipient without permission.
examples: A $33000.00 wire was confirmed received by the recipient despite his claim otherwise, but the receiving bank cannot recall the funds without his permission, which he refuses to give.
Chase accepted a wire transfer into an account that doesn't allow incoming wires but never applied the funds or sent them back, despite more than a week of calls.

themes.name: Funds inaccessible or blocked for unclear reasons
themes.problem_statement: Funds (e.g., $4,000 payment) or temporary credits are reversed, held, or made inaccessible, leading to $0 available credit and interest charges.
themes.root_cause: Internal policies, such as fraud flags, risk holds, or system errors during dispute investigations, cause funds to be unexpectedly frozen or unavailable.
examples: Temporary credits were reversed while disputes and CFPB complaints remained pending, and four credit card accounts were closed before Chase completed a documented investigation of all disputed charges.
A confirmed $2,500.00 balance transfer has not appeared in the Chase account, and Chase is charging $54.00 in interest while requiring a wait until a set date for an investigation.

themes.name: Bank fails to recover/return funds
themes.problem_statement: Funds are not returned or recovered despite bank error, recipient rejection, or customer request.
themes.root_cause: Bank internal processes fail to recover misdirected funds, to process authorized fund returns, or to properly handle rejected/missing transfers.
examples: A wire transfer was erroneously credited by Chase to an unrelated third-party account, and despite multiple written demand letters, Chase has not initiated recovery or provided documentation.

Two domestic wire transfers never appeared in the customer's own Chase checking account; the brokerage says they were received by Chase under a different account number that Chase won't discuss or confirm.

themes.name: International payment held for sanctions screening
themes.problem_statement: International rent payments are blocked by an intermediary bank under US sanctions rules without confirming when or why they are held.
themes.root_cause: The sanctions screening process holds international funds without providing timely information or support for resolution to the customer.
examples: A rent payment sent from the customer's mother abroad was likely blocked by an intermediary bank under US sanctions rules, and the bank has not confirmed when or why.

themes.name: Customer funds misplaced or misapplied
themes.problem_statement: Customer funds are misplaced (e.g., sent to wrong state's unclaimed funds), missing from closed accounts, or frozen, causing unpaid mortgages.
themes.root_cause: Operational failure, administrative error, or strict policy prevents customer access to their own funds or misroutes them to incorrect programs.
examples: A cashier's check Chase reported as sent to Louisiana's unclaimed funds was actually found in Ohio's program, and Chase sent it there without any documentation to its members.
With funds frozen and no notice, mortgage and other automatic payments went unpaid, risking late penalties and credit damage for a family with an infant.

themes.name: Escrow or mortgage funds mishandled or misapplied
themes.problem_statement: Escrow or payoff funds (e.g., $230,000) are misapplied to the wrong loan, held for missing documents, or unrefunded, causing delinquent reporting.
themes.root_cause: Mort servicing or escrow department fails to properly account for, release, or apply customer funds during payoffs or escrow analysis.
examples: Funds in an escrow account were held because the bank claimed missing documentation (proof of insurance and property tax payments) that the customer states were sent months ago.
$1500.00 left in escrow at year end was supposed to be returned but was instead used to pay taxes, and only half of the escrow balance was refunded after removal.

themes.name: Upfront fees unrefunded for denied loans
themes.problem_statement: A customer paid $1,100 in upfront fees (appraisal, insurance) for a loan that was ultimately denied, and the fees were not refunded.
themes.root_cause: Policy or process does not provide for refunding upfront fees when a loan application is denied and related services are not completed.
examples: $1,100 was spent on a cashier's check, appraisal fee and insurance for a loan that was ultimately denied, and the services were never rendered.

themes.name: other: no_response_or_follow_up
themes.problem_statement: Statements about no response or follow up that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Promised document or check never received by mail
themes.problem_statement: A promised invoice, title, or tax document (e.g., 1099-C) never arrives by mail despite requests, preventing finalization of paid-off accounts.
themes.root_cause: Fulfillment processes for mailing checks, cards, forms, or letters fail without triggering an alert or follow-up to the customer.
examples: After a lease ended, a $1,900.00 tax and disposition fee bill was never sent as promised, though the customer requested an invoice before paying and offered to pay immediately upon receipt.
An auto loan paid off years ago still has no title provided by Chase, and a written request for leniency went unanswered.

themes.name: Promised callback or follow-up communication never occurs
themes.problem_statement: A customer is explicitly promised a callback or follow-up regarding declined payments, damaged currency, or account holds, but never hears back for weeks.
themes.root_cause: Employees or escalation teams fail to schedule or execute promised outgoing calls and communications within expected SLAs.
examples: A branch teller submitted an earlier payment incorrectly causing it to be declined, and complaints about it plus promised escalation callbacks were never returned.
Customer was told someone would call back within a few days regarding damaged currency, but no one called back after a few weeks.

themes.name: Prolonged investigation or freeze without updates
themes.problem_statement: Accounts are under investigation for up to six months with no updates, timelines, or explanations on when funds will be released.
themes.root_cause: Long-running fraud and account investigations lack automated status updates or service level agreements for proactive customer communication.
examples: Despite previous contact and submitted paperwork, no one followed up on the estate account for six months, leading to fears of getting the runaround.
After multiple calls and reaching the escalation team, the customer was repeatedly told there was no update and no timeline for when the funds would be deposited.

themes.name: Promised credit, refund, or bonus not applied
themes.problem_statement: A promised refund for late fees, a $200 savings bonus, or a dispute provisional credit is never applied despite agent assurances.
themes.root_cause: Manual crediting processes fail or are significantly delayed without proactive notification or tracking to ensure completion.
examples: A Chase representative said he processed a refund of 3 late fees and return-payment fees, but it was never done and there is no record of it.
A branch employee showed on his screen that the $200.00 savings bonus requirements were met and promised a follow-up email, but the bonus was never applied and no follow-up ever came.

themes.name: Submitted documents ignored or unacknowledged
themes.problem_statement: Required forms, trust documents, or police reports sent via fax or mail are not acknowledged or reviewed across multiple attempts.
themes.root_cause: Inbound documents (mail, fax, branch submissions) are lost, misrouted, or not correctly linked to the customer's existing profile or claim.
examples: Multiple trust documents sent to Chase were never acknowledged, reviewed, or responded to.
A faxed transcript and paperwork from the merchant confirming the fraud and refund was never received by Chase across three attempts at two different branches.

themes.name: Inaccessible communication channels for explanations
themes.problem_statement: Customers cannot get explanations for denials or closures because departments do not take calls/emails or require branch visits while abroad.
themes.root_cause: Processes lack accessible communication channels or transparency, blocking customers from reaching specialized teams for explanations.
examples: He asked for documentation explaining the denial but was told the department handling it does not take calls or emails and he would need to visit a branch.
Secure Message support said the case needed a specialized team and told the customer to call, but Chase has not confirmed the case was forwarded while the customer is abroad.

themes.name: Customer repeatedly transferred between departments
themes.problem_statement: Customers are repeatedly transferred or ping-ponged between different bank departments or merchants without their fraud or fee issue being resolved.
themes.root_cause: Internal hand-off processes between departments or external referral protocols are inefficient or unclear, leading to infinite loops and unresolved issues.
examples: Chase and the merchant repeatedly told her to contact each other without resolving the fraud claim or reopening the case despite her providing evidence.
The bank said to dispute the charges with the wallet provider, but the provider said it could not dispute third-party purchases and to go back to the bank.

themes.name: Delayed or inadequate fraud alerts
themes.problem_statement: The bank delays notifying a customer of confirmed fraud for over ten days, relying on mailed letters instead of immediate calls or texts.
themes.root_cause: The fraud alert system relies on slow communication channels (e.g., mail) for critical notifications, delaying the customer's ability to respond.
examples: Chase knew a scammer was draining the business account starting days earlier, but chose to alert by mailed letter that arrived over ten days later instead of calling, texting, or emailing.

themes.name: Account actions taken without prior notice
themes.problem_statement: The bank closes accounts or reverses disputed rent overcharges (e.g., $580) without prior notice or giving the customer a chance to submit proof.
themes.root_cause: Automated or manual account action triggers lack a notification or justification process, impacting the customer's account status unexpectedly.
examples: Chase closed all the accounts without prior notice while the customer was trying to cash a pending reimbursement check.
A disputed $580.00 rent overcharge was reversed by Chase with no notice or chance to submit documentation, overdrawing the account.

themes.name: Vendor unresponsive after payment
themes.problem_statement: A customer pays $450 for a service or insurance through the bank, but the third-party vendor becomes unresponsive after scheduling.
themes.root_cause: Payment facilitation does not include mechanisms to ensure service delivery or responsiveness from third-party vendors post-payment.
examples: Paid $160.00 for a driving-lessons coupon plus $290.00 for insurance, but the company offered a class date over a month out and then stopped responding to calls and messages.

themes.name: Refusal to provide requested account documentation
themes.problem_statement: The bank refuses to provide account records, transaction details, or written explanations regarding account alterations, denials, or closed complaints.
themes.root_cause: Policies or a lack of streamlined processes prevent sharing internal records, evidence, or detailed rationales directly with the customer.

themes.root_cause: A background data synchronization process or system bug erroneously overwrites manual customer updates with outdated or default information from legacy databases.
examples: Chase has turned the mortgage automatic payment feature back on at least 4 times, but its system keeps turning it off again.
An incorrect address, still shown by one of three credit bureaus, keeps automatically overwriting manual corrections on the account every few months.

themes.name: Account lockout after contact info change
themes.problem_statement: Customers are locked out of their accounts for weeks after changing their phone number or email, as they can no longer receive verification codes to log in.
themes.root_cause: The authentication system lacks a secure fallback method for identity verification when a customer updates their primary contact information, causing access loops.
examples: After changing phone number, the customer has been unable to access online accounts even after waiting 15 days for verification to take effect.
An email says the account email was changed per a request the customer never made, but there is no way to call or reply since fixing it requires a working phone.

themes.name: other: fraud_not_stopped_or_not_refunded
themes.problem_statement: Statements about fraud not stopped or not refunded that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Scammer impersonates bank to steal credentials
themes.problem_statement: Customer receives a spoofed call from a scammer impersonating the bank's fraud department, tricking them into providing passwords and SSNs.
themes.root_cause: Fraudsters utilize caller ID spoofing and social engineering to impersonate bank staff and bypass customer security awareness.
examples: The agent requested the customer's account number and online banking password for identity verification, and the customer provided this sensitive information.
Customer received a suspicious phone call from someone claiming to be from Union Financial's fraud department, asking for full security number, birthdate, and address.

themes.name: Fraud claim denied because PIN or credentials used
themes.problem_statement: Bank denies refunds for ATM robberies or stolen replacement cards, citing that the use of a PIN or credentials makes the transactions authorized.
themes.root_cause: Fraud investigators rigidly classify any transaction using a valid PIN or credential as authorized, even when police reports prove theft or duress.
examples: Money forced out at an ATM by armed robbers, with a police report filed, was denied a refund because Chase said entering the PIN under duress disqualifies reimbursement until suspects are prosecuted.

An identity thief who ordered a replacement debit card and set her own PIN spent $1600.00 in debit card purchases that Chase still calls authorized, despite video evidence of her picking up the card and a filed police re

themes.name: Temporary fraud credit withdrawn after review
themes.problem_statement: The bank issues a temporary credit for reported fraudulent transactions but later reverses the credit after re-investigation.
themes.root_cause: Secondary fraud investigations conclude there is insufficient evidence of fraud or deem the transaction legitimate, triggering a clawback of funds.
examples: After a phone and wallet theft abroad led to $870.00 in fraudulent ATM, purchase and transfer transactions, Chase issued a temporary credit but then withdrew it days later after review.

Two unauthorized debit charges totaling $960.00 were reversed and then charged back because the merchandise was 'received,' even though a thief simply printed the invoice and picked it up in person without ever showing I

themes.name: Fraudulent account opened or large withdrawals made
themes.problem_statement: Identity thieves open large fraudulent accounts or make large unauthorized withdrawals, sometimes involving elder abuse.
themes.root_cause: Identity verification checks fail to detect stolen personal information during account opening, or systems fail to flag anomalous large withdrawals.
examples: A $64,000.00 auto finance account was opened without her knowledge or a contractual agreement, and she keeps receiving messages threatening to affect her credit.
An account was opened in the customer's name without their knowledge or consent, discovered through a letter in the mail.

themes.name: Fraud monitoring failed to stop unauthorized transfers
themes.problem_statement: Unauthorized transfers or automatic payments clear the customer's account, causing overdraft fees and raising elder financial abuse concerns.
themes.root_cause: Fraud monitoring algorithms fail to flag or block anomalous, unauthorized transactions or automatic payments on the customer's account.
examples: A $500 transaction made on January 1st from the customer's account was not authorized and the recipient is not recognized.
An overdraft fee was charged for an automatic payment that the customer did not authorize and suspects is due to someone hacking her account.

themes.name: Inconsistent decisions on related fraud claims
themes.problem_statement: The bank approves small fraud claims but denies larger related claims from the exact same scam or incident.
themes.root_cause: Different investigators review related claims in isolation, or strict dollar-value thresholds trigger different investigation criteria and outcomes.
examples: Of two fraud claims for the same incident, one for $490.00 was credited back, but the other for $1,700.00 was reversed because Chase says it was the customer.
Of several claims filed for payments to the same crypto scam, Chase refunded only the smallest ($1,000.00) and denied the larger $1,800.00 and $2,100.00 debit claims and $6,200.00 in wire transfers.

themes.name: compromised or altered check processed
themes.problem_statement: The bank processed and cleared a forged, altered, or fraudulent check without detecting the issues.
themes.root_cause: Bank's check processing systems or personnel failed to detect alterations, forged signatures, or missing endorsements.
examples: The account was overdrawn by a check the customer never wrote, which someone printed at a branch using only a single form of ID, and a Counter Fee was charged for it.

A bleached and fraudulently renamed rent check deposited without detection was promised reimbursement within 14 days, but the claim was later denied for a time lapse with no defined deadline ever given.

themes.name: Bank fails to freeze account after fraud reported
themes.problem_statement: Despite the customer reporting fraud, the bank fails to freeze the account or stop pending transactions, allowing further unauthorized wires.
themes.root_cause: Operational delays or system limitations prevent immediate application of account freezes or cancellation of pending transfers upon fraud report.
examples: A replacement debit card was intercepted before delivery and used to withdraw $4500.00; the bank refused to cancel the transaction while it was still pending and later denied the fraud claim.
A fraudulent wire was sent from the account after Chase told the customer their accounts were frozen following a report that the phone was stolen.

themes.name: Bank authorized scammer requests for cards or cash
themes.problem_statement: The bank mails replacement cards to unverified overseas addresses or allows a thief with a fake ID to withdraw large sums of cash in person.
themes.root_cause: Staff or automated systems fail to properly verify identity when processing replacement card requests to new addresses or large cash withdrawals.
examples: Chase sent replacement debit cards twice to an overseas address not on my file, and roughly 40+ foreign purchases followed, yet Chase claims I made them.
The imposter made 42 unauthorized transactions totaling $17,000.00 using the replacement card, and Chase denied all the fraud claims.

themes.name: coerced transfer or investment scam not refunded
themes.problem_statement: The customer was scammed into making voluntary transfers (e.g., crypto, investment, romance), and the bank denied the claim.
themes.root_cause: Bank policy considers transfers authorized by the customer, even under coercion or false pretenses, as ineligible for fraud reimbursement.
examples: After a scammer who hacked the customer's accounts coerced bank transfers and $35000.00 in cryptocurrency payments through a fake romantic relationship, Chase denied the dispute in favor of the scammer.
Fraud alerts were triggered during three coerced cash withdrawals totaling $21,500.00, but a bank manager overrode them and gave the cash to a customer under duress from an impersonation scam.

themes.name: Bank refuses to open fraud claim for ACH transfers
themes.problem_statement: The bank refuses to investigate or open a fraud claim for large unauthorized ACH withdrawals or debits, leaving funds unrecovered.
themes.root_cause: Staff incorrectly interpret dispute policies or system limitations prevent the initiation of fraud claims for non-card ACH transfer types.
examples: An ACH debit payment made to a company that never delivered the purchased item was not refunded, and Chase said it cannot file a claim for ACH debit payments.
Four unauthorized ACH withdrawals totaling $14,000.00 were made to cryptocurrency platforms I never dealt with, and Chase refuses to retrieve the funds as the merchant instructed.

themes.name: Bank refuses to refund stolen or altered check
themes.problem_statement: Customer checks are stolen, altered, and cashed, but the bank denies the refund claim, sometimes citing 60-day time limits.
themes.root_cause: The bank rigidly enforces time limits on forged check claims or places liability on the customer despite clear evidence of alteration and theft.
examples: After a $550.00 check was fraudulently cashed under the customer's name, they were told they'd get the money back, then later told they never would.
A $2000.00 rent check was fraudulently altered and rewritten to a different payee, but the claim was denied because more than 60 days had passed since the incident.

themes.name: fraud claim denied despite evidence or lack of proof
themes.problem_statement: The bank denied the customer's fraud claim, citing a lack of proof, or ignored evidence like police reports provided by the customer.
themes.root_cause: The bank's investigation process demands an excessively high burden of proof and easily dismisses customer-provided evidence.
examples: Money deposited into the new account before it was ever used was found to be stolen, but the fraud claim was denied for lack of evidence.
Someone requested a card replacement under the customer's name and made 10 withdrawals, but the claim was declined for lack of proof it was not the customer.

themes.name: Fraud claim denied due to prior merchant history
themes.problem_statement: The bank denies fraud claims for large unauthorized transfers because the customer had an unrelated prior transaction with the merchant.
themes.root_cause: Fraud investigators incorrectly assume that a prior legitimate transaction with a merchant implies blanket authorization for all future transactions.
examples: A $3,500.00 ACH debit paid a credit card the customer does not own, and Chase denied the fraud claim by pointing to a $110.00 transaction to the same card that was also unauthorized.

Someone hacked the account and made $2000.00 in unauthorized payments to a crypto platform, but Chase denied the refund citing a past account there even though details like the phone number did not match.

themes.name: Forged or altered check processed and cleared
themes.problem_statement: Stolen and altered checks for large amounts are processed and cleared from the account without detection.
themes.root_cause: Teller verification procedures or automated check scanning systems fail to detect forged signatures, altered payees, or duplicate charges.
examples: Fake checks debited the account multiple times totaling $7200.00, none of which appeared on statements, and Chase's executive department refused to pay while threatening collections for any further recourse.
A $22,000.00 check mailed via USPS was stolen, altered to a different payee, and cleared from the account before anything was traced or recovered.

themes.name: fraud claim denied because customer participated in scam
themes.problem_statement: The bank denied the fraud claim because the customer physically made the withdrawal or authorized the transfer while being scammed.
themes.root_cause: Bank policies exclude from fraud protection any transaction where the customer actively participated, even if induced by deception or coercion.
examples: Scammers posing as Chase convinced the customer to withdraw $1,000.00 in cash for a fraudulent transfer, and Chase denied the dispute saying the withdrawal was authorized.

Scammers posing as Chase employees convinced her to deposit $23,000.00 in person into a Chase account they controlled to 'protect' her funds, and $20,000.00 remains recoverable but Chase says it is not liable since it wa

themes.name: Scam transaction denied refund as authorized
themes.problem_statement: The bank denies refunds for massive losses from job or check scams, classifying the transactions as authorized by the customer.
themes.root_cause: The investigation concludes the transaction is authorized because the customer physically initiated the transfer, even under the influence of a scam.
examples: A counterfeit check scam impersonating a school research position led to $3500.00 leaving the account, but Chase misclassified the claims as an account compromise and denied them as authorized transactions.
Unauthorized XXXX withdrawals totaling $28,000.00 were made from the checking account, and after reporting the fraud Chase wrongfully denied the reimbursement claim.

themes.name: Required provisional fraud credit missing or delayed
themes.problem_statement: The bank fails to issue Regulation E provisional credit within the required 10 days of a reported fraud dispute, with investigations dragging on for months.
themes.root_cause: Claims processing backlogs or procedural failures prevent the timely issuance of provisional credits mandated by Regulation E deadlines.
examples: Despite reporting $510.00 in fraud the same evening and freezing the card, Chase denied reimbursement claiming authorization and never issued the Regulation E provisional credit.
Chase did not provide the provisional credit required within 10 days of the dispute and, 131 days later, still has not resolved the investigation or issued written findings.

themes.name: Fraud claim denied claiming customer received benefit
themes.problem_statement: Bank denies unauthorized transaction claims, arguing the customer received a benefit or because the scammer used the customer's mailing address.
themes.root_cause: Investigators wrongly use matching shipping addresses or unrelated purchases at the same location as definitive proof the customer benefited.
examples: An $800.00 charge at a bakery hundreds of miles away was ruled a valid transaction because the customer had separately bought a water bottle from a stadium vendor.
A $2,000.00 unauthorized transaction claim was denied because the customer allegedly 'received benefit from this transaction,' despite it being unauthorized fraud.

themes.name: Fraud claim denied despite evidence or police report
themes.problem_statement: Fraud claims of up to $11,000 are denied despite customers providing police reports, FTC affidavits, and clear evidence of unauthorized transactions.
themes.root_cause: Fraud investigators rigidly apply dispute policies and disregard customer-provided documentation of theft or location.
examples: A fraud dispute for over $11,000.00 was denied despite a police report, an FTC Identity Theft Affidavit, and evidence the transactions occurred online without the customer's involvement.
A merchant made numerous small unauthorized recurring charges after an initial $1.00 test payment, and Chase refused to refund any of them, citing its dispute policy.

themes.name: Stolen reward points not restored after account breach
themes.problem_statement: Bank restores stolen cash but refuses to reinstate reward points (up to $1,300) fraudulently redeemed for gift cards or orders during an account breach.
themes.root_cause: Fraud policies treat reward points differently from cash or assume redemption is authorized if initiated via a compromised linked email or account.
examples: Reward points from two long-held credit cards were redeemed for gift cards at the same time as other fraudulent transactions, but Chase concluded the customer benefited and took no further action.

After a confirmed account breach, Chase restored stolen bank funds but refused to reinstate about $1300.00 in credit card reward points that were fraudulently redeemed into gift cards during the same incident.

themes.name: Fraud charges on canceled or misdelivered replacement cards
themes.problem_statement: Over $3,200 in fraud occurs when replacement cards are sent to old addresses, intercepted, or when canceled card numbers are successfully charged weeks later.
themes.root_cause: Systems fail to invalidate canceled card numbers or send pre-activated replacements without adequately verifying the delivery address.
examples: Chase sent pre-activated replacement credit cards to an old address without canceling the originals, leading to over $3200.00 in fraudulent charges.
A merchant was allowed to charge a credit card number that had already been reported lost and canceled 3 weeks earlier, and Chase treats the resulting charge as valid.

themes.name: scam payment claim denied as self-authorized
themes.problem_statement: Bank denied the customer's claim for money lost to a scammer (e.g. for goods, services, or fake support).
themes.root_cause: Fraud policies classify customer-initiated transfers to scammers as authorized transactions, excluding them from unauthorized fraud protections.
examples: A fake ticket seller impersonating someone who does not exist took a $200.00 Zelle payment and disappeared, and Chase said it could not help since the customer sent the money herself.
$900.00 sent to a scam concert ticket seller through a peer-to-peer payment app was never returned, and both the bank and the app said they could not reverse the payment.

themes.name: P2P transfer recovery denied without investigation
themes.problem_statement: Customers are told recovering lost funds from P2P platforms is impossible and discrepancies are not investigated, even for transfers sent to mistyped phone numbers.
themes.root_cause: Institution policy dictates P2P transfers are final, leading agents to summarily declare recovery impossible without conducting a detailed investigation.
examples: A transfer sent to a mistyped phone number, though displaying the correct recipient name, was repeatedly said to be expedited with the money coming back, but the claim was ultimately closed and denied.
Reported transaction discrepancies were not adequately investigated, and the customer was told recovering lost funds was impossible and tracking the transactions unfeasible.

themes.name: Scam claim denied because transfer was customer-initiated
themes.problem_statement: Fraud claims up to $990 for scams (fake tech support, crypto, fake merchants) are denied because the customer authorized the initial P2P or debit transfer.
themes.root_cause: Fraud rules automatically categorize transactions as authorized if initiated by the customer, even when induced by deceptive scams.
examples: A scammer posing as tech support guided the customer to move $990.00 through a fraudulent prepaid debit card scheme, and the bank refused to help recover the funds or file a dispute.
A crypto transaction authorized under false pretenses due to a scam resulted in a total loss, and Chase denied the fraud claim despite a police report being filed.

themes.name: other: policy_or_terms_change
themes.problem_statement: Statements about policy or terms change that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Account closed or locked without warning
themes.problem_statement: Checking or savings accounts are suddenly closed, frozen, or locked without prior notice, blocking paycheck deposits and causing rent delays.
themes.root_cause: Risk, fraud, or compliance operations close accounts based on internal flags without proactively communicating the reason to the customer.
examples: The checking account was closed without prior notification, blocking a paycheck deposit and causing the customer to fall behind on rent.
Chase closed the checking account without authorization, further complicating the ability to get information about the refund status.

themes.name: Credit limit significantly decreased without warning
themes.problem_statement: A credit card limit is suddenly reduced to an unusable level (e.g., $3,000) overnight without warning, severely impacting the customer's credit score.
themes.root_cause: Automated risk models trigger a credit line decrease based on credit profile changes or utilization, without providing advance warning.
examples: The credit limit on the Amazon Chase card was reduced to an unusable level while a billing-error arbitration and a dispute affidavit were still pending and unrebutted.
A credit limit was cut by a large amount overnight with no justification, tanking the credit score, despite over two decades of on-time, above-minimum payments.

themes.name: In-person branch visit strictly required
themes.problem_statement: A customer is required to visit a branch over two hours away just to get a bank statement, keep an account, or set up power of attorney.
themes.root_cause: Security or identity verification policies strictly mandate in-person branch visits for certain account transactions or changes, with no remote options.
examples: Customer needs a copy of last month's bank statement but the bank's security policy prevents emailing it, requiring an in-person branch visit.
The customer needs to set up power of attorney for their father's account but cannot come to a branch, and the bank requires mailed forms with notarized signatures, which the customer finds too slow.

themes.name: Promotional offer or bonus terms altered or not honored
themes.problem_statement: A loyal customer cannot get a promotional savings interest rate or extend an expiring credit card rate because the offer expired or terms changed.
themes.root_cause: Marketing or rewards policy enforcement applies strict, undisclosed, or changed criteria that disqualify the customer from receiving the expected offer.
examples: A loyal existing customer found she was not eligible for a higher interest rate promotion on savings accounts, which had expired and was only for new customers, leading to a feeling of unfairness.
The savings account interest rate promotion expired last month, and the bank stated it cannot be extended.

themes.name: Unexpected fees from undisclosed date and schedule policies
themes.problem_statement: Customers are charged unexpected fees or penalties because weekend due date rules, grace periods, and new fees are not clearly disclosed before being applied to their loans or leases.
themes.root_cause: Fee calculation policies, such as weekend processing rules and advance payment requirements, are not clearly displayed in contracts or proactively communicated to customers.
examples: Chase requires auto loan payments 3 business days before a due date that falls on a Sunday or be penalized, a policy the customer says isn't clearly disclosed.

When the lease payment due date falls on a weekend, Chase requires the funds to be available before the due date rather than the next business day after, a requirement not stated in the signed lease contract.

themes.name: Rewards points permanently forfeited upon account closure
themes.problem_statement: Customers lose large amounts of accumulated rewards points (e.g., $1,400) without warning or a redemption grace period when a single credit card account is closed.
themes.root_cause: Account closure policies automatically and permanently erase accumulated rewards points without providing proactive warnings, transfer options, or a grace period.
examples: Closing a single Chase credit card resulted in the forfeiture of accumulated Ultimate Rewards points, without any disclosure during the closure call that this would happen.
Chase closed the account without direct email or mail notice, instead posting the closure notice six clicks deep in an online portal section, causing forfeiture of over $1400.00 in rewards points.

themes.name: Service refused when declining sensitive phone verification
themes.problem_statement: Customers cannot receive phone assistance or complete transactions like wire transfers because they are unwilling to provide their full Social Security Number for identity verification.
themes.root_cause: Phone authentication protocols strictly require a full Social Security Number for verification and do not offer secure, flexible alternative methods.
examples: Customer cannot complete a wire transfer because they are unwilling to provide their Social Security Number over the phone for verification, as required by bank policy.
The customer was uncomfortable sharing their Social Security Number over the phone for identity verification, which prevented the agent from accessing the account and providing personalized advice.

themes.name: Unexpected mortgage payment increase from escrow or rate
themes.problem_statement: Customers face unexpected mortgage payment increases (e.g., jumping by $250) due to delayed escrow shortage recalculations or adjustable interest rate hikes.
themes.root_cause: Automated escrow analysis cycles are delayed after insurance changes, or variable rate adjustments occur without adequate proactive customer notification.
examples: The interest rate on the adjustable-rate mortgage went up, causing higher monthly payments that the customer is worried about affording.
After failing to collect my mortgage payment twice, Chase diverted part of a $970.00 payment into an escrow account it unilaterally established, then raised my payment to over $1,100.00.

themes.name: Denied loan modification or hardship payment plan
themes.problem_statement: Customers experiencing job loss or financial hardship are denied affordable repayment plans or loan modifications, resulting in late payment reporting and damaged credit.
themes.root_cause: Financial hardship program policies have rigid eligibility criteria that restrict agents from offering custom loan modifications or temporary relief plans.
examples: Customer is two months behind on mortgage payments due to job loss and is seeking options like a loan modification to reduce monthly payments.
During a government-shutdown-caused job loss, no affordable payment option was offered, resulting in late payment reporting that is now hurting the credit score and access to financing.

themes.name: Removal of preferred online payment methods
themes.problem_statement: Customers are unable to pay their credit card balances online because the options to use an external checking account or debit card have been disabled or removed.
themes.root_cause: System updates or payment processing policies have deprecated specific external payment methods, disabling debit card or external checking account options.
examples: Chase disabled the ability to connect an external checking account to pay the credit card balance, forcing payments to keep coming from the overdrawn account.
Chase removed the option to pay with a debit card online, which the customer believes was done deliberately.

themes.name: Co-signer required despite good credit and steady income
themes.problem_statement: Customers with good credit and steady income are confused and frustrated when their loan applications are flagged to require a co-signer.
themes.root_cause: Automated underwriting rules trigger rigid co-signer requirements based on specific thresholds without allowing manual override for strong individual financial histories.
examples: Customer's loan application requires a co-signer despite good credit and steady income, and they do not understand the reason for this bank policy.

themes.name: Denied or overly complex loan due date modification
themes.problem_statement: Customers are denied simple requests to change their loan due dates or face burdensome new documentation and financial explanation requirements to do so.
themes.root_cause: Servicing policies strictly limit due date changes or mandate excessive hardship documentation, removing agents' ability to process simple schedule adjustments.
examples: The customer's request to modify loan due dates was denied due to bank policy.
The bank's policy for modifying loan due dates changed, requiring new documentation and a detailed explanation of financial situation, which the customer provided previously.

themes.name: Non-negotiable interest rates on repayment plans
themes.problem_statement: Customers willing to pay off their debt cannot afford the offered non-negotiable interest rates (e.g., 6% or 12%) or rigid system-generated repayment terms.
themes.root_cause: Risk assessment software locks in strict, automated interest rates and repayment structures, providing no override permissions for customized negotiations.
examples: The customer is confused about the 12% APR interest rate terms for their $10,000 line of credit and wants to negotiate it down, but is informed it is non-negotiable.
The offered system-generated 6% rate plan would leave the customer, whose net monthly profit is about $3500.00, unable to afford the payments despite offering to repay the full principal.

themes.name: Refusal to waive valid late or over-limit fees
themes.problem_statement: Customers request waivers for steep fees, such as a $35 late fee or $40 over-limit fee, but agents strictly refuse to reverse them as a one-time courtesy.
themes.root_cause: Customer service policies strictly prohibit agents from issuing courtesy waivers for correctly assessed late or over-limit fees.
examples: The customer finds the $35 late fee and $40 over-limit fee for the line of credit steep and asks if they can be waived, but policies are strict.

themes.name: other: staff_attitude_or_competence
themes.problem_statement: Statements about staff attitude or competence that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Staff exhibit rude, rushed, or disrespectful behavior
themes.problem_statement: Customers experience rude and dismissive behavior from staff, such as being repeatedly interrupted, rushed through transactions, or made to feel like a bother.
themes.root_cause: Frontline staff lack adequate de-escalation and soft-skills training, or are pressured by aggressive handle-time metrics that discourage patient service.
examples: Representatives were rude, interrupted repeatedly, and refused to take a delivery tracking number that would have helped locate the payoff check.
Teller Emantha at the Main Street branch seemed annoyed and rushed a check deposit transaction after a 30-minute wait, without greeting the customer.

themes.name: Representative deliberately disconnected the call
themes.problem_statement: Customers are deliberately hung up on by frustrated customer service representatives while trying to resolve account restrictions or title delays.
themes.root_cause: Representatives intentionally terminate difficult calls to avoid complex problem-solving or to manipulate average handle time metrics.
examples: Two Chase representatives disconnected the call while the customer was trying to resolve the title delay.
Chase customer service hung up on the customer twice out of frustration and was disrespectful while discussing the restriction.

themes.name: Customer treated with hostility or accused of fraud
themes.problem_statement: Customers are treated like criminals, called liars regarding scams, or have security called on them despite providing documentation proving transactions are legitimate.
themes.root_cause: Overly aggressive fraud prevention protocols and lack of empathy training lead staff to treat legitimate customers with unwarranted suspicion and hostility.
examples: When she visited a different branch, staff insisted she speak to a specific banker by phone, called security when she refused, and a false theft claim was later reported about her.
The bank noted in the customer's account that they were lying about the scam situation, despite the customer insisting this is false.

themes.name: Staff provide conflicting or shifting explanations
themes.problem_statement: Customers receive contradictory and constantly changing reasons for account restrictions, check holds, or clawbacks from multiple dismissive representatives.
themes.root_cause: Staff lack a standardized knowledge base and fabricate or guess explanations to dismiss customers when complex issues lack clear system documentation.
examples: A manager was extremely rude on the phone and gave contradictory reasons for the restriction, first blaming the phone number and then falsely claiming the fiance had not signed the check.
A representative unprofessionally blamed the customer for the clawback and gave shifting reasons - first calling the claim counterfeit, then invalid - without documentation.

themes.name: Staff refuse to assist, investigate, or process request
themes.problem_statement: Customers encounter staff who outright refuse to process payments, investigate issues, or assist with setting up specialized accounts like custodial or non-profit options.
themes.root_cause: Staff rigidly adhere to overly restrictive policies or lack the empowerment, knowledge, and willingness to navigate complex customer requests.
examples: A teller refused to let a longtime customer with a perfect payment history make an auto loan and credit card payment, saying the bank decided never to do business with him for life.
Customer had an unhelpful call last week about non-profit banking options, causing frustration and a need to repeat information and call again.

themes.name: Customers experience racial profiling or discrimination
themes.problem_statement: Customers feel targeted, denied funds, or have police called on them due to suspected racial profiling and discrimination based on race, gender, or nationality.
themes.root_cause: Implicit biases or a lack of adequate diversity and sensitivity training cause staff to apply security scrutiny disproportionately and treat minority customers poorly.
examples: The customer felt subjected to discrimination as a young Black man while being given a run-around instead of having their funds released.
The employee treated the customer's wife with suspicion and asked about her visa status after learning they had just returned from XXXX.

themes.name: Difficult communication due to strong staff accents
themes.problem_statement: Customers find it difficult and frustrating to communicate with call center representatives or resolve claims due to language barriers and strong accents.
themes.root_cause: The bank heavily relies on overseas call centers where staff lack sufficient language proficiency or neutral accents to clearly handle complex customer inquiries.
examples: A language barrier with overseas representatives made it difficult to get another claim opened after the first was closed.
The customer had difficulty communicating with call center representatives due to their accents, calling the overall phone experience hard to believe.

themes.name: Staff lack product knowledge or provide incorrect info
themes.problem_statement: Customers are given incorrect information about escrow accounts, points valuation (e.g., 1.5x travel points), or transaction details by unknowledgeable staff.
themes.root_cause: Staff receive inadequate training on specific product features, rewards systems, and policies, leading to factual errors during customer interactions.
examples: When escalated, the Chase Travel manager simply suggested cashing out the points at a much lower value and seemed unaware that points are worth 1.5x through Chase Travel.
A branch representative told a colleague the customer had typed in the wrong recipient number, which the customer says is not what he told him.

themes.name: Harassing or excessive collection contact by staff
themes.problem_statement: Customers, their families, and employers receive excessive, threatening, or harassing collection calls and in-person visits despite repeated requests to stop.
themes.root_cause: Aggressive debt collection practices and incentive structures prioritize contact volume over strict compliance with customer cease-communication requests.
examples: The collector makes incessant harassment calls to the customer, their employer's office workers, colleagues, and family members using spoofed or auto-dialed numbers.
A representative from a debt collection law firm knocked on the customer's door and threatened to return in a week if the full amount wasn't paid, while the firm never answers phone calls.

themes.name: Unfair treatment due to discriminatory bias or profiling
themes.problem_statement: Customers face invasive questioning, refused wire transfers (e.g., $6,500), and microaggressions regarding ethnic names or citizenship status, which they attribute to bias.
themes.root_cause: Staff harbor conscious or unconscious biases, improperly applying risk profiling rules based on customer age, ethnicity, or appearance rather than facts.
examples: A $6,500.00 international wire transfer was refused for two days despite sufficient funds and documentation, following invasive questioning the customer attributes to discriminatory profiling based on appearance.

After resubmitting a complete package, Chase asked for an explanation of variations in the customer's name on the credit report, which the customer felt was a microaggression tied to having an ethnic name.

themes.name: Staff exposed or mishandled sensitive personal info
themes.problem_statement: Bank staff improperly handle or expose customers' sensitive data, such as entering external debit card numbers or revealing SSNs and $25,000 account details to strangers.
themes.root_cause: Staff disregard data privacy protocols, lack training on secure handling of PII, or fail to secure physical environments during confidential customer consultations.
examples: While cashing a check, a branch employee keyed in the customer's full debit card number and expiration date from another bank and said the back office keeps it in case of fraud.
A manager interrupted a private consultation, brought an unauthorized stranger into the room, and exposed the customer's Social Security number and $25,000.00 account details.

themes.name: other: repeated_contact_needed
themes.problem_statement: Statements about repeated contact needed that fit no specific theme.
themes.root_cause: unassigned or low-confidence rows

themes.name: Endless loops in identity and account verification
themes.problem_statement: Customers face prolonged, repetitive identity verification hurdles—such as uploading IDs or multi-step checks—just to get basic interest rates or reorder checkbooks.
themes.root_cause: The authentication system routinely rejects valid inputs or applies overly strict security rules, trapping customers in verification failure loops.
examples: The customer experienced a frustrating and prolonged identity verification process, requiring account number, social security number, and an online driver's license upload.
